# 1 Enoch Chapter 101 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn (Aramaic) | **Section:** Epistle of Enoch

---

**1** Examine the heaven, you children of heaven, and every work of the Most High, and fear Him and do no evil in His presence.

**2** If He closes the windows of heaven and withholds the rain and the dew from descending on the earth on your account, what will you do?

**3** And if He sends His anger upon you because of your deeds, you cannot petition Him; for you have spoken proud and insolent words against His righteousness: therefore you shall have no peace.

**4** Do you not see the sailors of the ships, how their ships are tossed to and fro by the waves and shaken by the winds and are in great distress?

**5** And therefore they fear, because all their goodly possessions go upon the sea with them, and they have an evil foreboding of heart that the sea will swallow them and they will perish in it.

**6** Is not the entire sea and all its waters, and all its movements, the work of the Most High, and has He not set limits to its doings and confined it throughout by the sand?

**7** And at His rebuke it is afraid and dries up, and all its fish die and all that is in it; but you sinners who are on the earth fear Him not.

**8** Has He not made the heaven and the earth and all that is in them? Who has given understanding and wisdom to everything that moves on the earth and in the sea?

**9** Do not the sailors of the ships fear the sea? Yet sinners fear not the Most High.

---

*LOGOS notes: Chapter 101 is a nature argument: the sea obeys God (v. 7), even non-believing sailors fear the sea (vv. 4–5), so sinners have no excuse not to fear God. The argument from lesser to greater (qal va-homer) is a common Second Temple rhetorical form. The chapter is transitional — after the woe oracles, it introduces a final appeal to reason before the consolation section.*
